task.title: Flow text into columns
task.shortdesc: A multi-column element flows its content down a first column, then down the next one, and so on, as a newspaper does. You choose the number of columns or their width, the space between them and a line to draw there. The columns reference lists the properties used here.

image.alt: A box with a heading across its whole width. Under it, three columns of lines of text, with a vertical rule in the gap between the first and the second column and between the second and the third.

context.p: The element names in the examples, such as article, are placeholders. Use the names that occur in your XML.

step.cmd: Choose the number or the width of the columns

info.p: Set column-count on a block element to divide its content into that number of columns:

Set column-width instead to give the least width of a column. The element gets as many columns of that width as fit, and the columns are widened to fill the element. When you give both, column-count is the most columns that you get. The shorthand columns sets both: columns: 3 and columns: 12em are valid.

step.cmd: Set the gap and the rule

info.p: column-gap is the space between two columns. Its initial value, normal, is 1em. column-rule draws a line in the middle of each gap, with the width, the style and the color of a border:
A rule is drawn only between two columns that have content.

step.cmd: Balance the columns or fill them one by one

info.p: By default, the columns of an element are as even as they can be, so the text is shared in equal parts. column-fill: auto fills each column up to the height of the element, or to the bottom of the page when the element has no height, before it starts the next column:

step.cmd: Let a heading go across the columns

info.p: A block element inside the multi-column element can have column-span: all. It is as wide as the element, and the content before it and the content after it are laid out in columns of their own:
When the content is longer than the page, the columns go on to the next page. Each page has its own columns, and the text reads in order through all of them.

The columns follow the writing mode. In vertical lines, the columns are one above the other, and the lines of each column are as long as a column is tall. A vertical element inside horizontal text takes the height you give it; without one, CSSMedia sizes it and sets a long text in columns by itself. explains writing modes and boxes of another writing mode.

result.p: The content of your element flows into columns.
